correctness.rationale: For the complex smooth parameter range lambda outside {-2,-1,2}, direct partial derivatives prove smoothness. Restriction of the quartic to sixteen explicit lines gives exact squares, so these are bitangents. The complementary twelve coordinate-supported lines follow from a separable quadratic in their squared slope and the classical count of 28 distinct bitangents. Every possible triple concurrence is a determinant zero. A complete exact expansion of 560 determinants (24 identically zero) has only the stated irreducible factors; all nonsingular wall fibers are checked by exact quotient-ring pair incidence, yielding every n2,n3,n4 in the table and no multiplicity >=5. The standalone checker executed successfully with only integer polynomials; no extrapolation from samples or approximate roots.

value.rationale: The sixteen non-coordinate bitangents are a natural complete octahedral-symmetry-stable complement within a classical family of 28-bitangent arrangements. The exact incidence matroid/discriminant for every smooth parameter is an unsupplied structural classification, with emergent triple-point loci and distinct wall multiplicities that cannot be deduced from existing special-fiber profiles or the general quadruple lower bound. This precise invariant is useful for studying line-arrangement geometry and varies nontrivially even among smooth symmetric quartics; no downstream freeness result is asserted.
